source.title: Overcoming Overfitting and Large Weight Update Problem in Linear Rectifiers: Thresholded Exponential Rectified Linear Units

record.tranche_reason: Reports training and validation behavior for fully connected networks on MNIST, an alternate setting for the broader training claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative accuracy and loss outcomes for 8-, 20-, and 56-layer networks. These results do not test the specific CIFAR, shortcut, initialization, learning-rate, or normalization comparisons in the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The experiments compare activation functions in batch-normalized MNIST fully connected networks and report generalization behavior. They do not measure any version's specified effect. Batch normalization is used in the proposed method's evaluation; the qualitative statement that it improves TERELU performance establishes neither faster training nor higher learning-rate tolerance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that TERELU reduces large weight updates, stabilizes training, and improves generalization in shallow and deep networks. The reported experiments provide qualitative activation comparisons, rather than direct measurements of the proposed weight-update mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares activation functions in batch-normalized fully connected MNIST networks, rather than the listed CIFAR, width, shortcut, initialization, learning-rate, or batch-normalization comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: At 8 and 20 layers, ELU and TERELU are described as performing almost similarly; at 56 layers, the reported overfitting behavior differs.

fits_no_version.finding: ELU and TERELU reportedly perform similarly at 8 and 20 layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The reported activation-function performance difference depends on network depth in these MNIST fully connected networks.

fits_no_version.finding: At 56 layers, ELU reportedly overfits, while TERELU has matching training and validation accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation choice changes reported generalization behavior in the tested 56-layer batch-normalized MNIST network.

fits_no_version.finding: ELU validation loss reportedly stops decreasing after a few iterations, while TERELU validation loss continues decreasing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation choice changes the validation-loss trajectory in the tested 56-layer network.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 7.1 states that TERELU performs better with batch normalization, without quantifying the outcome or reporting training speed or learning-rate tolerance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization improves unspecified TERELU performance in the reported MNIST setting.

record.problems: The reported outcomes are qualitative and the accuracy and loss values are not stated in the text. No uncertainty estimates or explicit training-error values are provided.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large CIFAR convolutional networks, including random or corrupted labels and the specified training recipes.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-related training-error degradation in plain convolutional networks, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Initialization-dependent training speed, signal and gradient propagation, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Recovery, curvature changes, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Faster accuracy gains and higher learning-rate tolerance from batch normalization, and comparable training with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable numerical curves. No numerical training-error or convergence-speed result can be inferred from those captions. The qualitative batch-normalization performance statement does not establish V6's specified outcomes.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100, convolutional networks, random or corrupted labels, model size, and SGD or Adam recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Batch-normalized convolutional networks, residual shortcuts, and the stated initialization-based exceptions.
Initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and very deep plain networks.
Learning rates relative to stability limits, loss curvature or sharpness, and divergence.
Batch normalization versus no batch normalization as a controlled comparison, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.
